scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026: 610, 590) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026: 1180, 1260) (E-02).
Median dispute response time is 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets (E-01).
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03).
Of disputed bills in the Aug-Sep breakdown, 1240 carry read_type ESTIMATED and 1785 carry read_type ACTUAL (E-04).
No tariff/rate change occurred this year, per billing-db's tariff_change_log (E-06).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun–Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug–Sep 2026) (E-02), not because response handling is slow (E-01 shows median/p90 times within the 3.0-day SLA), but at least partly because field manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 accounts in Aug–Sep (E-03), forcing estimate substitution that accounts for the 1240 ESTIMATED-read-type disputed bills (E-04). This mechanism does not explain the majority of disputes, which involve ACTUAL-read-type bills (1785/3025, E-04) whose cause is not yet established (tariff change ruled out, E-06).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-03 revised by E-12: Still shows: manual-read route completion for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, a real field-collection shortfall. No longer means: this shortfall is the mechanism forcing estimate substitution for the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, since E-12 shows 1184 of those bills had an AMI read received before cutoff and were rejected on billing import, not missing due to field lateness.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Dispute response times across 2440 tickets are median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both within the 3.0-day SLA.

F-02.statement: Monthly dispute volume rose from ~600 (Jun-Jul 2026: 610, 590) to ~1220 (Aug-Sep 2026: 1180, 1260), roughly doubling.

F-03.statement: Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-04.statement: Of disputed bills in the billing-db breakdown, 1240 have read_type ESTIMATED.

F-05.statement: Of disputed bills in the billing-db breakdown, 1785 have read_type ACTUAL.

F-06.statement: Billing-db's tariff_change_log contains 0 records, confirming no tariff change occurred this year.

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-08.statement: route-log.lagging_routes returned 14 records with fields completion and route; sample record shows completion 0.70 for route R-00.

F-09.statement: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 records with fields account_id and route; route has 40 distinct values.

F-10.statement: Of AMI read events behind disputed ESTIMATED-type bills, 1184 were received before cutoff but rejected on billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had NO_READ_RECEIVED.

F-11.statement: Billing-config's validation_rule_changes log lists rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value with 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling: none) deployed 2026-08-01, and rule BV-09 (label text change) deployed 2026-03-02.

F-12.statement: mdms-export.meter_firmware_units shows firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) uses register_unit '0.1 m3' while firmware v3.x uses register_unit 'm3', a tenfold scaling difference between firmware versions.

F-13.statement: billing-db.affected_accounts_v42 lists 1184 distinct accounts, all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, and import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

F-14.statement: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts returned 1184 records, all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, matching billing-db's affected_accounts_v42 (E-15) account-for-account on these fields.

F-15.statement: billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed independently confirms 1184 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (firmware v4.2) with import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION and 56 (mixed firmware) with NO_READ_RECEIVED, matching E-12's breakdown.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-REQUESTER-RESPONSE-SPEED.statement: The August-September dispute surge is primarily a response-handling capacity problem: tickets pile up/escalate because Customer Service cannot answer fast enough, and an AI auto-answer agent would resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August is incorrectly rejecting valid reads or triggering wrong estimate substitution, producing systematically wrong bills and the dispute surge.

H-AMI-FEED-FAILURE.statement: The AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) from ORG-AMI is failing or delivering invalid reads since August, forcing estimate substitution and causing incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service (H-FIELD-BILL) have become incomplete or late since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-DEFECT.statement: The billing system's estimate-substitution logic (used when no accepted read exists) is itself flawed or overused, independent of upstream read quality, causing wrong bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-DEFECT.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry ACTUAL read type, suggesting a defect unrelated to estimate substitution — such as tariff/rate application or actual-read-to-bill calculation errors — drives most disputes.

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw AMI register value directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), deployed 2026-08-01 coinciding with the dispute surge onset (E-02); this unit mismatch is a plausible specific cause of the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION billing-import rejections identified in E-12.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data show dispute response times (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days) are within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, meaning response handling is not currently breaching its target even amid the surge; this undercuts the idea that slow answering is driving the dispute volume increase.

The CRM tool data confirms the dispute surge's magnitude and timing: volume roughly doubled from ~600/month in June-July 2026 to ~1220/month in August-September 2026, matching CL-01's 'doubled since August' framing numerically, but the record contains only aggregate monthly counts with no breakdown by cause, read type, or response speed.

Field route-log data show manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 manual-read accounts during Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a meaningful shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge window. This is consistent with (but does not alone prove) incomplete manual reads forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

Still shows: manual-read route completion for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, a real field-collection shortfall. No longer means: this shortfall is the mechanism forcing estimate substitution for the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills, since E-12 shows 1184 of those bills had an AMI read received before cutoff and were rejected on billing import, not missing due to field lateness.

Billing-db shows disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type, meaning a majority (1785/3025, ~59%) of disputes involve bills built from actual meter reads, not estimate substitution. This means the estimate-substitution causal chain (AMI feed failure, field-read degradation, estimate logic defect, rule-change rejections) can at most explain the smaller ESTIMATED share and leaves most of the dispute surge unaccounted for.

Still shows: disputed bills split 1240 ESTIMATED vs 1785 ACTUAL read type (3025 total). No longer means: that the 1240 ESTIMATED-type bills resulted from an absent read via field-route lateness or AMI feed failure; E-12 shows only 56 of the 1240 genuinely had no read, while 1184 had a read received before cutoff but rejected during billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is an unverified stakeholder statement, not confirmed by any authoritative billing-db record yet, and if true it would rule out a tariff/rate-change as the source of actual-read billing errors.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, authoritatively confirming no tariff/rate change occurred this year. This corroborates the prior stakeholder claim (CL-02) and interview-based evidence (E-05), and rules out a tariff/rate change as the mechanism behind the actual-read-majority dispute pattern noted in E-04.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative interview) claims field service has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills; this is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a possible mechanism for incomplete manual reads, not confirmed route-log timing or staffing data.

Still shows: SH-FIELD's unverified claim that field service has been short three readers since July, causing late routes and estimated bills, as a stakeholder statement. No longer means: a credible mechanism for the 1240 ESTIMATED-dispute bills, since E-12 shows 1184/1240 had an AMI read received before cutoff but were rejected on billing import, leaving only 56 with no read at all.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility may request route priority changes but execution requires Field Operations Manager confirmation, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update. It bears on authorization procedure only, not on the cause of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 individual routes with per-route completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving route-level granularity underneath the aggregate 0.88 Aug-Sep completion shortfall (E-03). It is a route-level dataset only — it carries no account identifiers or dispute linkage, so it is a precursor input for the planned join against billing-db:accounts_estimated_last_cycle (W-WI-1-ROUTE-DISPUTE-JOIN), not a completed account-level correlation.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-10 (billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle) lists 320 accounts estimated in the last billing cycle, with only account_id and route fields (40 distinct routes), e.g. AC-20000 on R-00. This is the account-level dataset needed to join against route-log:lagging_routes (E-09, 14 lagging routes) per work item W-WI-1-ROUTE-DISPUTE-JOIN, but by itself carries no dispute or completion-rate information and does not yet establish whether the route shortfall population overlaps with disputed accounts.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside has just been provisioned, citing vendor ticket TX-4471; this speaks only to whether the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query can now be retried, not to any causal fact about disputes, and is unconfirmed by a successful tool call or an updated mdms-export tool_health (still DEGRADED).

For the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-type bills, mdms-export shows 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected during billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (exported_to_billing=true), while only 56 had genuinely NO_READ_RECEIVED. This means the dominant mechanism forcing estimate substitution for ESTIMATED-type disputes is a billing-import rule rejecting valid high-consumption AMI reads, not absence of a read from field-route lateness or AMI feed failure.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: Billing-config's validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw AMI register value against 12-month m3 history, with unit_scaling "none") was deployed 2026-08-01 — the exact start of the Aug-Sep dispute surge (E-02) — while the only other change, BV-09, is an unrelated label-text edit from March. This gives a timing-matched, specific defect mechanism (a unit-scaling gap in a new validation rule) that plausibly produces the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION billing-import rejections E-12 found behind the 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-type disputes, and potentially affects other read types processed through the same billing-import validation step.

mdms-export.meter_firmware_units shows firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports register values in units of 0.1 m3 while firmware v3.x reports in plain m3, a tenfold scaling difference. Combined with E-12's firmware=v4.2 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections and E-13's BV-17 rule (deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling='none'), this confirms a concrete mechanism: BV-17 compares raw v4.2 register values (numerically 10x true consumption) directly against m3-based history, producing false high-consumption rejections.

E-16.content: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts → 1184 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'ami_read_ts', 'bill_read_type', 'firmware', 'import_status'] | account_id: 1184 distinct values | ami_read_ts: 540 distinct values | bill_read_type: ESTIMATED×1184 | firmware: v4.2×1184 | import_status: REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION×1184 | sample: {"account_id": "AC-10000", "ami_read_ts": "2026-09-01T02:00:00", "bill_read_type": "ESTIMATED", "firmware": "v4.2", "import_status": "REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: mdms-export.reads_for_accounts (E-16) independently returns the same 1184-account population as billing-db's affected_accounts_v42 (E-15): all firmware v4.2, bill_read_type ESTIMATED, import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, providing the AMI-side half of the account-level join needed for the rebill-backlog list (W-REBILL-BACKLOG). It does not add new accounts or a new mechanism beyond E-12/E-13/E-14/E-15.

E-17 (billing-db.import_status_estimated_disputed) independently reproduces, from the billing-db side, the same split already found in mdms-export's E-12: 1184 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (firmware v4.2) rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 (mixed firmware) with import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED. This is a second, source-independent confirmation of the BV-17 rejection mechanism, not a new finding.

U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-CAUSE.question: What specific mechanism (billing calculation error, usage estimation issue, or other defect) causes the majority of disputes on ACTUAL-read-type bills, given tariff change is ruled out?
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Resolving this determines whether a billing-calculation or rule defect, not field/estimate substitution, is the dominant cause; without it, any proposed fix for the majority of disputes is unfounded.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Correlate billing-db disputed ACTUAL-read bills with billing-config's import validation rule change log around August to isolate a specific calculation or rule defect.
U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue read-only diagnostic correlation and report findings to SH-BILL; issue no bill adjustment until a specific defect is confirmed and Billing Operations authorizes correction under K-BILLWRITE.

U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-ACCOUNT-OVERLA.question: Does the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95, 9200 accounts) match, at account level, the population generating ESTIMATED-read-type disputed tickets?
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-ACCOUNT-OVERLA.decision_impact: Confirms or weakens whether restoring route completion would actually reduce the ESTIMATED-read dispute population, informing whether push_route_update is a sufficient remedy.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-ACCOUNT-OVERLA.resolution_path: Perform an account-level join between the Aug-Sep route-completion-shortfall accounts (E-03) and the ESTIMATED-read-type disputed-ticket accounts (E-04) using route-log and billing-db.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-ACCOUNT-OVERLA.safe_placeholder: Treat the route-completion and ESTIMATED-read dispute populations as correlated but unconfirmed; do not restrict diagnostic or route-restoration scope to only the overlapping subset.

U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-DEFECT-RESO.question: Is reducing dispute ticket count via faster/templated answers a valid proxy for resolving the underlying bill-defect problem, or could it mask continuing incorrect billing while ticket counts drop?
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-DEFECT-RESO.decision_impact: If ticket count were used as the sole success signal, templated responses could suppress volume without fixing the ACTUAL-read defect, falsely signaling success.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-DEFECT-RESO.resolution_path: Track dispute volume (M-DISPUTE-VOLUME-TREND) jointly with the ACTUAL-read dispute share metric (M-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-SHARE) so volume reduction is corroborated by defect-rate evidence, not ticket count alone.
U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-DEFECT-RESO.safe_placeholder: Use response templates only for triage/communication quality, not as evidence of root-cause resolution; require corroborating billing-db defect data before declaring the dispute surge resolved.

U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE.question: What specific mechanism causes the majority of disputes on ACTUAL-read-type bills (1785/3025, E-04), given tariff change is ruled out (E-06)?
U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether any further remedy beyond the BV-17 fix is needed to bring dispute volume to baseline; without it the larger dispute share stays unexplained.
U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE.resolution_path: Run a billing-db reconciliation of billed amounts vs. expected usage*tariff calculation for the 1785 ACTUAL-read-type disputed bills, cross-checked against the billing-config rule change log.
U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Treat diagnose_actual_read_bill_defect as a read-only investigation; do not attribute ACTUAL-read disputes to the BV-17/firmware mechanism and do not propose any bill write until a corroborated cause is documented.

U-TICKET-PROXY-VALIDITY.question: Is reducing dispute ticket count via faster/templated answers a valid proxy for resolving the underlying bill defect, or could it mask continuing incorrect billing while ticket counts drop?
U-TICKET-PROXY-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If ticket count alone is used to judge success, the templates could suppress complaints without the billing defects actually being fixed, defeating G-1.
U-TICKET-PROXY-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Track M-BV17-REJECTION-SHARE and M-ACTUAL-READ-DISPUTE-SHARE alongside M-DISPUTE-VOLUME-TREND so template rollout cannot substitute for defect-resolution evidence.
U-TICKET-PROXY-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Ship draft_dispute_response_templates only as a communication aid; do not treat a reduced ticket count as evidence the underlying billing defects are fixed.

U-BV17-POPULATION-SCOPE.question: Does the BV-17 unit-scaling defect also affect non-disputed v4.2-meter accounts or other read types processed through the same billing-import validation step, beyond the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-type bills?
U-BV17-POPULATION-SCOPE.decision_impact: Determines the true remediation scope and whether the fix must cover accounts that have not yet disputed a bill.
U-BV17-POPULATION-SCOPE.resolution_path: Query billing-db/mdms-export for v4.2-meter accounts and other read types processed through BV-17 beyond the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills to size the non-disputed affected population.
U-BV17-POPULATION-SCOPE.safe_placeholder: Treat the BV-17 fix as scoped to the diagnosed 1184 rejected reads until the broader population is queried; do not claim full remediation coverage.

U-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.question: Is billing-config's validation_rule_changes log (DA-RULES, completeness UNKNOWN) complete, or could other undocumented rule changes also contribute to the dispute surge?
U-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.decision_impact: If other undocumented changes exist, BV-17 alone may not be the complete billing-import mechanism driving the surge.
U-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.resolution_path: Cross-check billing-config's validation_rule_changes log against deployment/change-management records to confirm no undocumented rule changes exist.
U-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.safe_placeholder: Proceed with BV-17 as the primary documented defect while flagging that DA-RULES completeness is UNKNOWN, so other undocumented changes are not yet ruled out.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL nightly export handoff from ORG-AMI reliably delivered with semantically valid AMI register data, given its delivery_status and semantic_validity are both UNKNOWN?
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is unreliable, the AMI read data underlying both the BV-17 rejection diagnosis and any ACTUAL-read diagnosis could be incomplete or mis-timed.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Query mdms-export export-batch metadata and compare against billing-db import timestamps for a sample of accounts to confirm nightly export delivery and semantic correctness.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Continue using the already tool-validated mdms-export records (E-12, E-13, E-14; AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) for diagnosis; do not treat the H-MDMS-BILL handoff metadata itself as a causal fact until checked.

A-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP.statement: The accounts affected by the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (E-03) substantially overlap with the accounts generating ESTIMATED-read-type disputed tickets (E-04), though no account-level join has been performed.

A-STAFFING-CAUSE-PLAUSIBLE.statement: SH-FIELD's unverified claim of a three-reader shortage since July (E-07) is treated as plausible context for the route completion shortfall (E-03), not as confirmed fact.

A-BV17-FULL-ATTRIBUTION.statement: The timing/mechanism match between BV-17's deployment and the v4.2 firmware unit mismatch fully explains all 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections, though no per-account audit confirming each rejected read came from a v4.2 meter has been run.

A-NO-READ-SUBSET-UNRELATED.statement: The remaining 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED ESTIMATED-type disputes are assumed unrelated to the BV-17 mechanism and are not further diagnosed under this problem.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills

K-DISPATCH.description: Changes to field dispatch routes are executed only after runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (service contract §4.2).

K-BILLWRITE.description: Writes to customer bills (re-bill, credit) require Billing Operations authority; no automated bill writes.

DA-PUSH-ROUTE-UPDATE.subject: ORG-FIELD
conditions: Requires runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager before execution per service contract §4.2 (E-08).

SC-NO-UNAUTHORIZED-BILL-WRITES.statement: No automated bill adjustment is written without Billing Operations authority per K-BILLWRITE.
SC-NO-UNAUTHORIZED-BILL-WRITES.validation_method: Human Gate approval required before any write_bill_adjustment execution; audit against K-BILLWRITE.

SC-NO-UNCONFIRMED-ROUTE-PUSH.statement: No field dispatch route change is pushed without runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager per K-DISPATCH.
SC-NO-UNCONFIRMED-ROUTE-PUSH.threshold: 100% of push_route_update actions runtime-confirmed by SH-FIELD

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requests an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026: 610, 590) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026: 1180, 1260) (E-02).
Median dispute response time is 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets (E-01).

Of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills, 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 had NO_READ_RECEIVED (E-12).
Billing-config's validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 deployed 2026-08-01, comparing raw register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none' (E-13).
Firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report register values in '0.1 m3' units vs v3.x's plain 'm3' units, a tenfold scaling difference (E-14).

problem_definition.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02), not because response handling is slow (E-01: median 1.6d/p90 2.8d within 3.0d SLA) or a tariff change (E-06), but because billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report register values in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x's plain m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misclassifies valid on-time v4.2 reads as high-consumption and rejects them at import (E-12: 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills had an on-time read rejected this way), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills for those accounts. This explains the ESTIMATED-type share of disputes (1240/3025, E-04) but not the larger ACTUAL-type share (1785/3025, E-04), whose cause remains unestablished.

supervision.current_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-02), not because response handling is slow (E-01: median 1.6d/p90 2.8d within 3.0d SLA) or a tariff change (E-06), but because billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; firmware v4.2 meters (rolled out June 2026) report register values in 0.1 m3 units versus v3.x's plain m3 (E-14), so BV-17 misclassifies valid on-time v4.2 reads as high-consumption and rejects them at import (E-12: 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills had an on-time read rejected this way), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills for those accounts. This explains the ESTIMATED-type share of disputes (1240/3025, E-04) but not the larger ACTUAL-type share (1785/3025, E-04), whose cause remains unestablished. (v2, ACTIVE)

H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw AMI register value directly to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), deployed 2026-08-01 coinciding with the dispute surge onset (E-02); this unit mismatch is a plausible specific cause of the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION billing-import rejections identified in E-12. proposal.summary: The investigation found that the August-September dispute surge (doubling from ~600 to ~1220 tickets/month, E-02) was not caused by slow response handling (E-01) or a tariff change (E-06), nor fully by field route lateness as initially suggested (CL-01, CL-03/E-07, both later invalidated by E-12). Instead, for the 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED read type, 1184 had a valid on-time AMI read that was wrongly rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-12, confirmed independently by E-17), because validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw AMI register values to m3-based history with no unit scaling, while v4.2 meter firmware reports values in 0.1 m3 units — a tenfold mismatch (E-14). This defect, and only this defect, was addressed in this release: deterministic account-level identification of the 1184 affected accounts (E-15, E-16) and a cross-checked import-status report, routed to Billing Operations for manual re-bill/credit review (no automated bill writes, per constraint K-BILLWRITE). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because this diagnostic work (diagnose_billing_import_rejection_defect:DA-RULES scope) is complete and verified against the evidence, but the broader problem — the larger ACTUAL-read-type dispute share (1785/3025, E-04), the ticket-response-template workstream, and the actual firmware fix deployment — remain open or out of scope and are explicitly flagged as unresolved rather than silently dropped.
key_points: Problem evolved: the original requester framing (CL-01, response-speed/auto-fix AI agent) and the first problem definition PD-1@v1 (field route lateness causing estimate substitution, built on E-03/E-07) were both invalidated once E-12 showed 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-type disputes involved an on-time AMI read rejected at import, not a missing read.

Root cause of the diagnosed slice: rule BV-17 (E-13) lacks unit scaling for v4.2 firmware meters, which report in 0.1 m3 units (E-14), causing false high-consumption rejections (E-12, E-15, E-16, E-17) — this is hypothesis H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT, status SUPPORTED.

What was released: a deterministic, verified list of the 1184 affected accounts and an independent import-status cross-check, intended for manual Billing Operations re-bill/credit review (SR-BACKLOG-REBILL-QUEUE), not any automated bill write — consistent with the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE Gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with several unknowns/VOBs deferred as out-of-scope rather than resolved (U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE, U-TICKET-PROXY-VALIDITY, U-TICKET-VOLUME-VS-DEFECT-RESO, VOB-R-7), so the release is scoped narrowly to the diagnosed BV-17 defect rather than the full requested scope.
The actual BV-17 fix (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX) was judged not feasible within contest time and was not deployed or verified against success criterion SC-BV17-REJECTION-ELIMINATED.

The majority of disputes (1785/3025 ACTUAL-read-type, E-04) have no established cause; diagnose_actual_read_bill_defect:DA-BILL work is blocked by open HIGH-impact unknowns (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-DEFECT-CAUSE, VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-CAUSE) and excluded from this release.
